history.dynasty: Bushahr dynasty (Sarahan was a former Bushahr capital before the move to Rampur)
history.period: CONFLICT (verify): sources variously claim ~2000 years old, 11th-12th century, or 17th century (founder Raja Marh of Bushahr)
history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas of India, dedicated to Goddess Bhimakali, the presiding deity of the Bushahr region, at Sarahan in Shimla district. Legend holds that the ear of Goddess Sati fell here (some sources say the right arm). A striking example of Kath-Kuni (stone-and-wood) architecture with sloping slate roofs, carved wooden facades and a silver-plated idol, the complex has two main towers (an older one no longer used for worship and a newer one) plus shrines of Raghunath, Narsingh and Patal Bhairava; the top-storey idol is worshipped only at certain times of year. The royal family's palaces and a heritage museum adjoin the complex. A 1905 earthquake tilted the old tower, which straightened after a later tremor. Exact founding date is CONFLICTING across sources (verify).

name: Bhimakali Temple
town_description: Sarahan is a small town in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, at ~2,300 m altitude, and was a former capital of the Bushahr dynasty before the capital moved to Rampur. It is dominated by the Bhimakali temple complex and set amid deodar forests with views of the Shrikhand Mahadev peak. The town lies ~17 km off NH-5 at Jeori, ~160-180 km from Shimla. The CSV town field ('Sarahan (Bhimakali)') is correct; town set to 'Sarahan'.

travel.road: ~17 km off NH-5 at Jeori (Rampur side); regular buses/taxis from Shimla (~6-8 hrs) and Rampur (~1 hr)

visitor_information.best_time: March to November (late March-early November ideal); winters are cold with possible snow
